headline: Google Cloud's Agent Gateway, a traffic controller for AI agents that reads the two main agent protocols, is available in preview.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: the announcement dates from Google Cloud Next earlier this year and the 8 Oct piece is analysis of it.
importance_line: Companies building systems of several AI agents get a way to control which tools each agent may use, but the gateway is only a preview, details may change, and the claim that it is the first of its kind is Forkast's own.
summary: Forkast News reports in an analysis that Google's Agent Gateway, introduced at Google Cloud Next '26 and still in preview, understands the Model Context Protocol (MCP, a standard that connects AI agents to tools) and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, so companies can allow an agent only specific tool calls. This is older news: the announcement was made earlier this year, and Forkast says details may change before general release.
notes: Re-dated older news: the freshness date 22 Apr 2026 comes from SDxCentral's Google Cloud Next coverage, not from the Forkast article, which gives no date for the event.
